authority: Saved task-1 and mission acceptance; this file defines evidence exchange and does not amend the mission or its verifier.

sourceProvenance.scope: Initial Actor checkout; report files will be uncommitted task outputs. Final integrated source requires its own receipt.

refAvailability.scope: Actor local repository only; supplied refs preserved verbatim, not replaced with local HEAD
refAvailability.objects: Accepted and snapshot commits/trees were independently resolved directly; missing local ref names do not negate their object identities.

oracle.retention: Read Git object at runtime into isolated scratch; never retain a tracked oracle copy.

contentManifestEncoding.order: Exact entry order of the NUL-delimited ls-tree command, without resorting.
fields: lowercase SHA-256 ASCII of Git blob bytes
contentManifestEncoding.record: Concatenate five netstrings (decimal byte length, colon, field bytes, comma), then one LF. Hash the concatenation of records with SHA-256. Non-blob content hash is empty; accepted corpus has only blobs.
contentManifestEncoding.content: git cat-file --batch with the entry OIDs in manifest order; parse declared byte sizes, not lines. Symlink blob bytes are the target text, not referent bytes.

benchmarkCorpus.materialization: Isolated Git index/tree equal to accepted tree; all accepted paths, modes, blob bytes and symlink targets unchanged. New implementation/tests/evidence must not enter this benchmark tracked list.
benchmarkCorpus.candidateSubstitution: Execute an untracked scratch candidate outside the corpus, from the same corpus cwd; leave tracked scripts/harness/validate.sh at accepted bytes. Both scripts retain the same exclusion path. Verify corpus before and after each run.
benchmarkCorpus.dereferencedInputs: Record each tracked path as regular-file, link-to-file, link-to-directory, missing or other under the harness -f predicate; hash readable bytes actually scanned before/after, including link referents. Preserve and record symlink resolution. Do not materialize directory links as regular files or silently omit unreadable inputs.

observedInitialSymlinks.scope: Actor initial local checkout metadata, not a benchmark measurement

benchmarkCorpus.identitySeparation: Benchmark identity remains the accepted corpus even when candidate changes. Final integrated source identity records the final index/commit plus working-byte/mode manifest and candidate hash separately; never call the optimized tree the unchanged accepted corpus.

semantics.shell: Existing set -e and set -u; Bash 3.2-compatible indexed arrays and builtins only. Native BSD grep extended-regex behavior; no GNU-only or new regex engine assumptions.

selection.gitErrors: stderr suppressed; failure tolerated as original. Preserve Git quoting/config behavior and original line-delimited read semantics.
selection.mode: Only first argument exactly --staged changes selection; other first arguments retain their original printed Mode value.
selection.empty: Print existing No files to validate message, exit 0 before check labels or coverage.
selection.missing: Every check skips paths failing [ -f ]; symlinks to regular files are included, links to directories are skipped. File count is the selected list count, not eligible existing-file count.

semantics.reportOrder: Within each check: original FILES order, then original rule order, then grep matching-line order. Never report pattern-first batches directly.
semantics.count: Increment once for each file/rule with nonempty report matches, regardless of matching line count. Distinct overlapping rules each increment. Check 4 increments per oversized file; Check 5 increments once on missing Bun or nonzero coverage exit.
semantics.streams: Preserve stdout and stderr bytes independently including ANSI escape sequences, spacing, blank lines, messages, line numbers and binary-file reporting. No normalization. Cross-stream interleaving is not a substitute for per-stream equality.

checks.label: Hardcoded secrets
checks.eligible: Every selected existing -f path except these case exclusions; no source-extension restriction.
checks.engine: grep -qE trigger then grep -nE report, stderr suppressed. Preserve engine semantics without translating literal regex text.

ruleOrder.invariant: At least one trigger must match this same file before reporting the report-expression lines. A report-only line can appear alongside a different triggering line in that file. Triggers from other files must not activate it.

checks.label: Architecture layer violations (domain must be pure)

ruleOrder.filterScope: Only this rule; apply after the original line-number prefix as accepted grep pipeline does.

checks.label: File length cap
checks.lineCount: wc -l counts LF bytes; no implicit extra line for an unterminated last line. Preserve original space-stripped integer and strict lines > ceiling comparison. A batched wc implementation must discard total rows and preserve file mapping, order, missing-file behavior and ceiling lookup.

checks.label: Test coverage thresholds
checks.skip: Only SKIP_COVERAGE=1 skips and emits the existing warning. No skip in performance/full acceptance receipts.
checks.workspaceRoot: Keep WORKSPACE_ROOT when set; otherwise mktemp -d -t av-validate-workspaces-XXXXXX and export it.
checks.outcomes: Preserve Bun-missing, coverage-nonzero and coverage-success paths verbatim, including inherited Vitest wording. Coverage still runs after earlier violations.

semantics.messages: All info/ok/warn/violation text and final success/failure messages are the literals at the oracle path/revision/hash. Preserve check-specific success suppression and cumulative count behavior.
semantics.exits: 0 when the selected list is empty or all checks pass; 1 for accumulated violations. Compare incidental original shell/tool failure exits as observed; never coerce every failure to 1.
semantics.unusedHelper: check_pattern is declared but not invoked by the accepted five checks; its -P fallback is not the active-check engine.

implementation.selected: Sequential unchanged-pattern batches over exact eligible existing-file lists, cache results, then replay file/rule/line order through existing messages.
implementation.batching: No grep subprocess per file or per reported file. One eligible-list batch per expression when host argument limits permit; deterministic bounded chunks are allowed only to respect host argument limits and must retain the same semantics. Keep trigger/report data separately where required.
implementation.reuse: Bash, grep, wc/awk and dependency-free Bun tests; no manifest/lockfile/runtime-dependency additions.
notSelected: Parallel pattern workers: adds process coordination and ordering risk before a measured need.
Cache across executions or narrower default input: invalidates unchanged-corpus acceptance and can skip checks.

fixtureMatrix.isolation: Create deterministic Git fixtures under scratch/target or system temporary directory. Generate payloads at runtime; no tracked original script copy or literal violation corpus. Execute each oracle/candidate pair against the same fixture root, Git configuration, files and environment.
cases: Clean eligible files and clean files of every selected extension.
Each of nine secret expressions under the actual grep engine, including nonmatches/placeholders.
Each of three dangerous-command rules, both protected-branch triggers and trigger/report differences.
All five architecture rules, each non-domain layer directory, within-domain ./ imports filtered only by rule 1, overlapping first/legacy/Go matches.
500 versus 501 LF counts, empty files, final line lacking LF, long excluded test/declaration/generated/managed/canvas files.
Multiple files, rules, repeated lines and repeated occurrences on one line; assert file/rule/line output order and per-file/rule totals.
Every exact/glob exclusion with positive eligible controls; document that secret scanning still covers many files excluded by Check 4.
Tracked-but-locally-missing files; staged ACM additions/copies/modifications and omitted deletions; unstaged content behavior remains original.
All-tracked empty input, staged empty input and only-missing selected input; coverage invocation/early return observed separately.
Controlled successful coverage, nonzero coverage and Bun-missing cases without skip; coverage still invoked when earlier checks fail.
Explicit SKIP_COVERAGE=1 equivalence case only, never substituted for full acceptance.
Binary-like data, symlinks to files/directories and supported path punctuation/spaces to expose batched filename framing changes.
fixtureMatrix.coverageStub: Only inside equivalence fixtures; deterministic stdout/stderr/exit/invocation record. Never satisfy real coverage, Cargo or integrated harness acceptance with a stub.
fixtureMatrix.failPolicy: Any stream-byte/exit discrepancy fails equivalence. A theoretically positive expression not supported by the actual BSD engine must be recorded as such, not silently reinterpreted.

receiptContract.format: Compact UTF-8 JSON records; schemaVersion=1 and evidenceKind distinguish equivalence, timing, verification, review and closeout. Missing/unperformed values are null or explicitly not-collected, never invented zeros/passes.
receiptContract.commandEnvironment: Record effective relevant PATH, locale LANG/LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE, Git config affecting path quoting/order, SKIP_COVERAGE (explicit unset in full runs), WORKSPACE_ROOT, TMPDIR and Rust/Cargo overrides. Hash or describe unrelated environment without storing secrets. Record the actual values or absence used, not assumed defaults.
receiptContract.hostTools: OS/version/architecture and tool command paths plus version output for Bash, grep, Git, Bun, rustc, Cargo, cargo-llvm-cov; wc/awk implementation identity and matching llvm-cov/llvm-profdata when coverage is collected. Record competing verification processes or their absence and run sequence.
receiptContract.streams: SHA-256 over raw bytes, including empty streams; record byte lengths and exact raw diagnostic location. For fixtures, include oracle/candidate stream hashes, exits, byte-equality booleans and fixture-definition hash/ID. Do not strip colors, timestamps or paths to manufacture equivalence.
receiptContract.sourceBinding: Before/after index tree/manifest, working-byte/mode and dereferenced-input identities must agree for each scope. Record uncommitted final edits independently of HEAD and include test/preservation-source identities. Existing coverage inputIdentity(root).sha256 is retained but does not include validate.sh or scripts/harness tests and cannot alone bind final harness source.

timing.observer: External monotonic observer drains stdout/stderr concurrently without altering validator output. Record clock API and marker detection; no wall-clock subtraction for elapsed times.
boundaries: tStart: monotonic time immediately before spawning the command.
tCheck5: time the complete original Check 5/5 label is received on stdout. Record the label byte offset and read timestamp.
tEnd: time process exit and both streams are collected; record exit observation and stream-drain completion separately if different.

durationsSeconds.checks1to4: tCheck5 - tStart; includes startup/file-selection/output delivery, so the <20s bound covers the full observed prefix.
durationsSeconds.check5: tEnd - tCheck5; observed coverage phase including unchanged result/footer/process-drain overhead, explicitly label that inclusion.
durationsSeconds.total: tEnd - tStart; same observer/clock; must equal checks1to4 + check5 within stored precision.

timing.pass: A valid non-skipped candidate run on the unchanged accepted corpus has checks1to4 <20. Record original/candidate independently and all attempted runs; do not omit a slow valid run. Gate success is separate from timing success.
timing.missingBoundary: Use null and explanation if Check 5 never starts (e.g. empty input or shell failure); do not claim zero time or complete performance acceptance.
timing.schedule: Serialize benchmark pairs and coverage collection; no competing expensive suites. Retain warm/cold/run order and actual repeated measurements when taken; this contract invents none.

receiptContract.diagnostics: Paths and SHA-256 for compact retained receipts/reports; point to existing ignored coverage runs/target or external scratch for large raw outputs, with retention/availability stated. Do not copy large native exports into harness-speed.
receiptContract.checkTimeout: Framework per-check limit is 1800000 ms. Mission planning timeoutMs=120000 does not authorize terminating checks at 120000; any new wrapper/replay must allow at least 1800000 ms. Report shorter existing nested deadlines to Chief rather than weakening or altering the operator verifier.
